findings.claim: The change raises MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth from 500 to 5000. This is a tenfold loosening of the recursion/depth limit that protects against stack overflow when deserializing untrusted data. It is unrelated to the requirement, which concerns a generator/analyzer crash. A deeply nested payload now gets through up to 5000 nested levels, and the default stack may be exhausted before the limit trips. That is an uncatchable StackOverflow crash (DoS).

receipt_plan.detail: Deserialize a payload nested about 4000 levels (e.g. arrays of arrays) with MessagePackSerializerOptions.Standard.WithSecurity(MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData). On the base build it throws InsufficientExecutionStackException at depth 500. On the head build it is accepted, or it overflows the stack on a small-stack thread. Also assert MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth == 500.

findings.claim: The reportDiagnostic wrapper silently drops any diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of the compilation. Several diagnostics are created with a null location, e.g. MemberNeedsKey, and for the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic, GetPropertyIdentifierLocation can now return null. A null location is Location.None, which is not in source. These diagnostics are discarded even for source types where the identifier cast fails, for example when the member is a field or the syntax is not a PropertyDeclarationSyntax. This can suppress user-protective diagnostics, such as MsgPack004 or the AOT key diagnostics, for source-declared members.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an analyzer test where a source-declared member that lacks a Key is declared in a way that produces a null location, e.g. a partial or primary-constructor-synthesized property. Assert that the diagnostic is still reported. Compare against the base build.
